q: 1. What is/are the Citizen's Charter's?
explain: A Citizen's Charter represents the commitment of an organization towards its citizens/clients regarding standard of services, information, choice, and grievance redress.

q: 2. Which is the first country in the world to incorporate 'Citizen Charter' in 1991 AD? (PSC-2081)
explain: The Citizen's Charter initiative was first launched in the United Kingdom by Prime Minister John Major in 1991.

q: 3. Who was the British Prime Minister when the Citizen Charter was issued?
explain: John Major introduced the concept to improve the quality of public services in 1991.

q: 4. Who was the Prime Minister when the Citizen Charter was re-launched in Britain?
explain: Tony Blair's government re-launched the program in 1998 under the name 'Service First'.

q: 5. The Citizen's Charter programs was re - launched in 1998 by Tony Blaire as -------
explain: In 1998, the program was rebranded as 'Service First' to emphasize responsiveness.

q: 6. Which Administration Reform Commission adopted the concept of public charter of Nepal?
explain: The High Level Administrative Reforms Commission of 2048 BS recommended the adoption of such charters in Nepal.

q: 7. Which one of the following is not basic element of the citizen charter?
options: Description of services being provided by department or agency
Promotion of various methods to get benefit from the services available
Provision for the inspection of the agency's work
explain: While transparency is key, 'expecting any public record' is generally a right under RTI, not a primary element defined within the charter itself.

q: 8. How many principles are there in Citizen's Charter?
explain: The original British model of the Citizen's Charter was founded on 6 key principles.

q: 9. Which of the following is not a principle of the Public Charter?
explain: Public charters focus on openness and transparency, making confidentiality the outlier.

q: 10. What is the main purpose of keeping a Public Charter in public offices?
explain: The charter is a tool for establishing good governance by making administration accountable to the public.

q: 11. What is the impact of a well-designed citizen charter on the relationship between the government or organization and its citizens?
options: It enhances trust and mutual respect
It improves the overall quality of services provided by the organization
explain: A clear charter builds trust, clarifies processes for citizens, and drives internal quality improvements.

q: 12. Among the following which is not mentioned in the citizens Charter's of a public agency of Nepal?
options: Service to be provided and time taken
explain: While the office and grievance officer are mentioned, providing every staff member's personal contact is not a standard requirement.

q: 13. When did the Citizen Charter begin in Nepal?
explain: The formal implementation of Citizen Charters in Nepal started in 2056 BS.

q: 14. Under which program was the Citizen Charter introduced in Nepal? (PSC-2076)
options: "Income for the poor, justice for the voiceless"
"Justice for the Voiceless, Income for the Indigents"
"Justice for the voiceless, income for the poor"
"Income for the poor, justice for the voiceless"
explain: It was introduced under the 'Justice for the Voiceless, Income for the Indigents' program.

q: 15. From which district did Nepal’s Digital Citizen Charter begin?
explain: The first digital version of the charter was piloted in Rukum.

q: 16. When did the Government of Nepal implement the Citizen Service Charter?
explain: A significant mandatory implementation phase occurred in 2061 B.S..

q: 17. When did the government of Nepal set up the one-stop service center?
explain: The one-stop service center was established on Jestha 1, 2076 BS.

q: 18. Since when was the Citizen Charter with compensation implemented in Nepal?
explain: Charters including compensation provisions for service failure began on Baishakh 2, 2070 BS.

q: 19. The Citizen Charter with compensation in Nepal... has the provision of compensation ranging from --------
explain: Compensation amounts are tiered between 250 and 5,000 Rupees depending on the service.

q: 20. Which office in Nepal was the first to implement a Citizen Charter with compensation?
explain: Several departments, including Immigration, Survey, and Foreign Employment, were part of the initial rollout.

q: 21. From which body did Nepal's Citizen Charter first originate?
options: Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration
explain: The OPMCM is the central body responsible for administrative reforms and the origin of the charter initiative.

q: 22. Which of the following are tools of good governance?
explain: Social Audits, Charters, and RTI are all mechanisms to ensure transparency and accountability.

q: 23. What is/are the shortcomings of Citizen's Charter's in Nepal?
explain: Implementation is often hindered by low awareness among citizens and overly complex bureaucratic procedures.

q: 24. The provision for citizen charter in public office is mentioned in? (PSC-2080)
explain: The Good Governance (Management and Operation) Act 2064 provides the primary legal basis.

q: 25. Which of the following is/are the principles of Citizen's Charter?
explain: Effective charters must be developed participatively, remain transparent, and set clear standards.

q: 26. Which of the following element(s) ensure the access to information and transparency?
explain: All listed options serve as tools to bring information and services closer to the citizen transparently.

q: 27. Citizen Charters includes -------
explain: A comprehensive charter lists the what, how much, and how of public service delivery.

q: 28. What are the main aspects of good Governance? 1. Accountability 2. Impunity 3. Transparency 4. Taxation
explain: Accountability (1) and Transparency (3) are fundamental pillars of good governance; impunity is the opposite.

q: 29. Which of the following is not a component of good governance?
explain: While sovereignty is a state feature, Rule of Law, Legitimacy, and Accountability are the procedural components of governance.

q: 30. Which of the following is/are the Major element(s) of the Citizen's Charter of Nepal?
explain: Nepal's charters must identify the responsible official, the grievance person, and the specific time for service.

q: 31. Quality, Choice, Standards are the ------- of Citizens' Charter.
explain: These are the core principles derived from the UK model to ensure citizen-centricity.

q: 32. What is called for the public service charter of Australia?
explain: Australia uses the term 'Service Charter' to define the relationship between agencies and the public.

q: 33. Which country initiated the "Service Standard Initiative" for Public Charter in public service delivery?
explain: Canada was a pioneer in developing the 'Service Standard Initiative' to measure and improve performance.

q: 34. In the context of good governance what does accountability denote? 1. People's influence on their rules 2. Working in accordance with rules and regulations 3. Effective control of people on their rules 4. Public's access to decision making
explain: Accountability involves adhering to legal frameworks (2) and ensuring the public can participate in/see the decision process (4).

q: 35. The concept of good governance was first raised in ------- five year plan.
explain: Nepal formally integrated good governance into its development planning starting with the 9th Five Year Plan.

q: 36. Which section of the Good Governance Act (Management & Operation Act) - 2064, has provisioned about the charter to be maintained in governmental office (public office)?
explain: Section 25 specifically mandates the display and maintenance of Citizen Charters.

q: 37. What is the main objective of Public Service Charter?
options: To provide information about service delivery to recipient
To publish the purpose of office
explain: The primary goal is informing the service recipient about what they are entitled to and how to get it.

q: 38. Which among the following are correct statement(s)? 1. The British Prime Minister John Major Implemented Citizen's Charter in U.K. 2. In Nepal, Concept of Citizen Charter came into practice in 2064 B.S.
explain: Statement 1 is correct (John Major, 1991). Statement 2 is incorrect as it started in Nepal earlier (2056 BS).

q: 39. Which among the Act has initiated the legal provision for the public service agencies in Nepal to have Citizens Charter's mandatory? (PSC-2078)
explain: The 2064 Act turned the previous administrative practices into a mandatory legal requirement.

q: 40. In which article of the Constitution of Nepal has provisioned the guarantee of the good governance?
explain: Article 51 contains state policies which include the commitment to ensuring good governance.

q: 41. The first country in the world to incorporate "Right to information" is:
explain: Sweden enacted the Freedom of the Press Act in 1766, the world's first RTI legislation.

q: 42. Which is the first country in SAARC region to incorporate "Right to Information" into its constitution?
explain: Nepal was the first in the SAARC region to provide constitutional recognition to RTI in 1990.

q: 43. 'Right to information' is provisioned in Article ------- of the Constitution of Nepal.
explain: Under the current Constitution of 2072 BS, RTI is a fundamental right guaranteed in Article 27.

q: 44. According to Good Governance Act-2064, what is/are the provision of Citizen's Charters to be maintained in public offices?
options: estimated time for delivery the service
particulars of the fees to be charged
explain: The Act requires full transparency regarding timeframes, costs, and potential remedies.

q: 45. In which act, the consideration about provision for public service charter is made? (PSC-2079)
explain: While related to RTI, the primary act managing the 'Public Service Charter' is the Good Governance Act.

q: 46. Who among the following is not required to be invited to a public hearing?
explain: Public hearings involve external stakeholders and experts; internal auditors are part of the internal control system, not the public forum.

q: 47. According to the Good Governance (Management and Operation) Act, 2064, which of the following is not included in the Citizen Charter?
options: Services provided by the concerned office and their nature
Procedures to be completed by the service recipient
Code of conduct for service-providing employees
explain: The charter focuses on external service delivery; codes of conduct are separate internal documents for employees.

q: 48. What is the primary responsibility of a service recipient seeking public services?
options: To gather information about the service from intermediaries
To request information from the office head
To visit the office with the help of local political leaders
To mandatorily study the Public Charter
explain: Citizens are encouraged to use the charter directly rather than relying on intermediaries or external influence.

q: 49. From which institution the concept of good governance has developed?
explain: The World Bank introduced the concept in 1989 as a prerequisite for development and aid.

q: 50. Which of the following is not included in a Public Charter?
options: Fees, time, and procedures for receiving services
Personal relationships between service recipients and providers
explain: The charter is a professional document; personal relationships are irrelevant and outside its scope.

q: 51. Which of the following is not part of a Public Charter?
options: Type, quantity, time, and responsible person for services
Address of the service-providing body or person
explain: A Public Charter focuses on the external outcomes and accountability mechanisms (what, where, when) rather than the internal organizational methods like group work dynamics.

q: 52. According to legal provisions, how often must government offices in Nepal conduct public hearings?
explain: The Good Governance Rules mandate that public offices should conduct public hearings every three months (trimesterly) to collect feedback on service delivery.

q: 53. Which of the following is/are public service(s)?
options: Services provided by the private sector
explain: Public service includes any service intended to serve all members of a community, whether provided by the state, private entities under regulation, or NGOs.

q: 54. According to the Good Governance (Management and Operation) Act, which of the following is the highest priority in a Citizen Charter?
options: Estimated time for delivering the service
Detail statement of service offered by the office and its nature
Description of the officer responsible for providing service and his/her chamber
Procedure to be followed by the service user (customer) to obtain the service
explain: The primary foundation of the charter is the clear declaration of exactly what services the office is mandated to provide and the nature of those services.

q: 55. What are the weaknesses of Nepal's Citizen Charter?
explain: Nepal faces implementation gaps due to a combination of citizens not knowing their rights (awareness) and the administration failing to simplify the path to those rights.

q: 56. Which of the following is not addressed in the Good Governance (Management and Operation) Act, 2064?
options: Responsibilities of ministers, secretaries, and department heads
explain: Investigation of corruption-related offenses is handled under the Prevention of Corruption Act and by the CIAA, not the Good Governance Act.

q: 57. Which of the following are legally mandated subjects to ensure good governance for the public? I. Provisions of Citizen Charter II. Provisions of Public hearing III. Provisions of Grievance Management IV. Provisions of Spokesperson
explain: The Good Governance Act 2064 explicitly mandates all four: Charters (Sec 25), Public Hearings (Sec 30), Grievance Handling (Sec 31), and Spokespersons (Rule 14).

q: 58. Under which section of the Good Governance Act, 2064 did the Government of Nepal exercise its authority to formulate the Good Governance Rules, 2065?
explain: Section 45 of the Act gives the government the power to frame rules for the effective implementation of the Act's provisions.

q: 59. The provision of Spokesperson is made on?
explain: The specific requirement for every office to designate a Spokesperson (Information Officer) is found in Rule 14 of the Good Governance Rules, 2065.

q: 60. In which section of Good Governance Act-2064, has provisioned about the "Conducting Public Hearings"? (PSC-2079)
explain: Section 30 of the Good Governance (Management and Operation) Act, 2064 makes public hearings mandatory to maintain transparency.
